title: Instance Grouped Robots by Material to Reduce Per-Frame JavaScript Overhead
hypothesis: Replacing 1600 separate Box meshes with two InstancedMeshes (one per color/material), while preserving the semantic identity of each robot through userData.semanticIds, will substantially reduce per-frame CPU update and render submission time, because Three.js will submit far fewer objects to the renderer, and matrix updates will be tight per-instance buffer writes instead of per-object allocations and update calls.
expectedEffect: Lower p95 JavaScript CPU time in both update and render submission, heightened performance stability, and unchanged visual, animation, and picking correctness.
notes: This replaces 1600 .add()-ed Meshes with two InstancedMeshes that preserve all per-robot animation and world-space transforms exactly, using per-instance matrices. Each instance has a unique semantic identity correctly available in userData.semanticIds, allowing interaction and picking code to translate instance ids to the original robot ids. All geometry, color, animation, and world space placement logic and deterministic update are preserved; the only change is batching by material.
